video.title: The Easiest Way To Start A Business That Almost Never Fails

summary: Chris Koerner interviews Spencer (Lonear Trash, Texas), a software founder who started a residential trash subscription business by pre-selling 3-month service to ~150-200 neighbours on Facebook after the incumbent hauler degraded. He bought a used under-CDL side-loader truck 100% financed, sourced used bins, and grew via referrals (free month per referral), Facebook ads (CAC $35-100), and branded bins. Claimed ~$50-60k/month revenue, ~$300k first-year revenue and ~40% margin on rough maths, with very low churn. They also discuss municipal truck auctions as a flip or list-selling side hustle, city contracts, and starting cheaper with bulk junk pickup.

speakers.name: Spencer Scott
speakers.description: Founder of Lonear Trash, a Texas residential trash subscription business; also runs software companies

ideas.name: Neighbourhood trash subscription (Lonear Trash)
ideas.one_liner: Pre-sell residential trash pickup subscriptions to a neighbourhood abandoned by a bad incumbent, then serve it with a financed used side-loader truck.
ideas.business_model: Subscription billed in 3-month increments per household
ideas.customer: Households in neighbourhoods (HOA/utility districts) in Texas unhappy with their existing trash hauler
ideas.problem: Incumbent hauler sold to private equity, service and billing got worse, and missed pickups
ideas.offer: Weekly trash pickup with provided branded bins; pre-sale with full refund if the 200-customer target is not hit

pricing.notes: Referrers get a free month per referred neighbour; refund guarantee on pre-sale.

acquisition_channels.details: Posted a no-risk pre-sale offer to the neighbourhood Facebook group; got ~150 sign-ups in 10-15 days and ~200 over about 45 days.

quote.text: we ended up getting I think in 15 days something like 150 people and then ended up getting like in the first year about 200
quote.speaker: Spencer

acquisition_channels.details: Free month of trash for each referral; one customer referred 16 houses and got a year free. Branded bins on the street act as billboards.

quote.text: we created a referral system that gave someone a free month of trash every single time they refer a neighbor
quote.speaker: Spencer

acquisition_channels.details: Facebook ads sending to Stripe checkout with a success page so the pixel tracks conversions; needed ~$300/day for about a week to train the algorithm; CAC ~$100 early, down to ~$35 some months.
Google pay-per-click; Spencer says he should have used Google Local Services Ads at ~$50/day (pay per lead) and collected Google reviews earlier.
Presence in HOA and utility district recommendations as new residents ask neighbours who to use.

ideas.delivery: Driver(s) collect bins weekly with an automated side-loader arm; ~400 houses in ~4 hours per truck with one dump trip. Two employees (a salaried main driver and a part-time driver). Trucks stored at an RV storage facility; bins in a storage unit.
unit_economics_claims: ~$50-60k/month revenue vs ~$30k costs, ~40% margin (Koerner's rough calc)
CAC $35-100 vs customer lifetime value ~$3,500 (Koerner estimate)
~1% monthly churn estimated, no cancellations due to service
First-year revenue ~$300k, little profit due to capex
ideas.startup_cost: Effectively no cash out of pocket: $15k pre-sales covered ~$10k used bins plus dump fees and fuel for 3 months; truck $35k + $5k shipping financed via a $40k Amex personal loan at ~7% over 10 years ($700/month).
ideas.time_to_first_revenue: Pre-sale cash within days of posting (about 10-15 days for 150 sign-ups)

acquisition.how: Facebook/Google ads and referral credits can be run by agents; community posting needs light human presence and Facebook group rules.

onboarding.how: Stripe checkout and CRM automation; address-based setup and bin delivery needs a human.

delivery.how: Physical trash collection with trucks and drivers; a human must do it each time.

billing.how: Stripe recurring quarterly billing is fully automatic.

support.how: Agents can handle missed-pickup and billing queries; physical fixes need humans.

uk_applicability.notes: UK household waste is collected by councils or licensed contractors under council contracts, so private residential subscription collection is not a standard market. Commercial waste needs a waste carrier licence and waste transfer notes. The pre-sale and referral mechanics transfer, but the specific business largely does not.

risks: Incumbent is not always bad; customers rarely switch without a trigger
Truck breakdowns, tyre wear, insurance cost
Sole reliance on drivers showing up

quotes.text: if I can get 200 customers to sign up, there's 400 people who live in here... And if you don't if we don't hit that number, 100% refund. There's no risk.
quotes.speaker: Spencer

quotes.text: I bought the truck, started making payments on it, never took a dollar out of my pocket.
quotes.speaker: Spencer

quotes.text: I can't win business just to win business... You have to mess up for me to win the business.
quotes.speaker: Spencer

ideas.name: Municipal garbage truck auction sourcing and flipping
ideas.one_liner: Buy used trash trucks cheaply at in-person city auctions, financing them, to use or resell.
ideas.business_model: Buy low at auction, keep or resell for profit
ideas.customer: Trash companies and operators wanting used trucks
ideas.problem: Used trucks are expensive; municipalities replace fleets on a schedule and sell them at auction
ideas.offer: Trucks purchased far below market and resold or refurbished

price_points.label: Spencer's winning bid for a 2020 truck

pricing.notes: Auction pay-in-cash requirement caught Spencer out; he used an equipment financing preapproval.

acquisition_channels.details: Municipal truck auctions found in trash truck Facebook groups and Marketplace.

ideas.delivery: Attend in-person auctions, transport, optionally refurbish via dealer, and list for sale.
unit_economics_claims: Bought a ~$190k truck for $60k at auction
ideas.startup_cost: About $10k cash suggested to attend an auction

acquisition.how: Auction discovery could be scraped by agents but buyers must attend in person.

uk_applicability.notes: UK councils and fleet operators sell vehicles via auction and online auction houses; discounts are likely smaller and the market is thinner.

quotes.text: if I would have just taken it right there and put it on Facebook Marketplace, it would have been worth 190.
quotes.speaker: Spencer

ideas.name: Municipal truck auction list
ideas.one_liner: Pay people to call municipalities for auction schedules and sell the compiled list of trucks.
ideas.business_model: Sell lists or subscription of auction inventory
ideas.customer: Trash operators and flippers wanting cheap used trucks
ideas.offer: Compiled list of upcoming municipal auctions and trucks

acquisition_channels.details: Sell into trash truck Facebook groups (implied).

ideas.delivery: Offshore VAs call municipalities and compile auction lists.

acquisition.how: Listing sold via community posts and SEO.

delivery.how: Agents can scrape council auction notices; some phone checks needed.

uk_applicability.notes: UK equivalents exist via council auction pages and auction houses; market smaller.

risks: Information is public so easy to copy

quotes.text: You just list it do the listing inventory listing. You don't even buy them, right? And then you sell the list.
quotes.speaker: Chris Koerner

ideas.name: Bulk junk and trash pickup with truck and trailer
ideas.one_liner: Start a junk-removal business with a pickup and trailer via Facebook, then upgrade to bag pickup and dumpsters.
ideas.problem: People need junk hauled to the landfill

pricing.notes: Spencer suggests the path: bulk pickup, trailer, drop-in dumpsters, then branded subscription bins.

ideas.delivery: Owner drives truck and trailer to the landfill.
ideas.startup_cost: Next to nothing if you own a pickup truck

uk_applicability.notes: Man-with-van and waste clearance is common in the UK but needs a waste carrier licence and licensed tip disposal.

quotes.text: I would start with bulk pickup. Facebook will pick up your trash. Then I would go to trailer.
quotes.speaker: Spencer

ideas.name: Wheelie bin cleaning service
ideas.one_liner: Power-wash customers' trash bins on a schedule, sold via Facebook ads.

acquisition_channels.details: Facebook ads with properly set-up conversion tracking; unit economics work according to Kade.

uk_applicability.notes: Bin cleaning businesses exist in the UK; water discharge rules apply.

quotes.text: I met a kid who was doing 50 grand a month power washing trash cans.
quotes.speaker: Spencer

ideas.name: Municipal waste contracts
ideas.one_liner: Scale up to winning city waste collection contracts with many thousands of homes.

acquisition_channels.details: Formal bids; only a few large firms typically win; Spencer has one micro-city contract.

unit_economics_claims: Two trucks serve ~20,000 homes per the former city manager

uk_applicability.notes: UK council waste contracts go through formal procurement and are dominated by large firms.

tactics.name: Risk-free neighbourhood pre-sale
steps: Identify a neighbourhood with a failing incumbent
Post a transparent offer on the local Facebook group with a target (e.g. 200 customers)
Offer 100% refund if the target is missed
Charge 3 months upfront ($105)
Extend Stripe payout hold to cover refunds
Use the cash to buy equipment

quote.text: We put in Stripe, you can extend the escrow before the money gets transferred to you.
quote.speaker: Spencer

tactics.name: Facebook ads conversion tracking setup
steps: Hire a Fiverr specialist to install the pixel
Send buyers to Stripe checkout, then to a success page
Optimise for conversions not clicks
Budget about $300/day for a week to train the algorithm
Scale spend as CAC falls

tactics.name: Referral credits
steps: Give a free month for each neighbour referred
Credit the account when the name is submitted

tactics.name: Leave branded bins at addresses
steps: Keep the address open when customers cancel
New residents call the number on the bin
Use branded bins as street billboards

tactics.name: Seed local Facebook groups
steps: Join 10-20 neighbourhood Facebook groups
Search for complaints about trash
Plant seeds, then launch when a contract fails

tactics.name: Find trucks in operator Facebook groups
steps: Join the Mom and Pop Trash group and truck Marketplace groups
Look for under-CDL side-loaders
Buy from a brand with local dealer support

tools_mentioned.name: Stripe
tools_mentioned.purpose: Payments, pre-sale checkout, extended payout hold

warnings.warning: Equipment financiers can be sharky: no early payoff, truck repossessed if you miss payments.

quote.text: it's a little sharky. Like, I would say be careful cuz I talked to like four other people.
quote.speaker: Spencer

warnings.warning: Auction requires cash on the day.
Parking a garbage truck at home triggers HOA letters.
Spencer did not collect Google reviews for the first 1.5 years, which he regards as a mistake.
Customers do not switch just because of the story or reviews; they switch when the incumbent errs.
Spent the pre-sale cash on bins rather than financing them.

lessons.lesson: Pre-sales with a refund guarantee de-risk a physical business and fund equipment.
Ignorance of an industry can be a superpower; industry insiders often discourage.

quote.text: Ignorance can be bliss. Naity can be a superpower.
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

lessons.lesson: Route density drives profitability in route-based services.
Subscription businesses are more sellable and have lower churn than per-job service businesses.
Let customers' recurring payments finance bulk purchases to preserve cash for marketing.
Switching depends on timing; be present when the incumbent fails.
Stop operating in the business and hire a driver to work on growth.
Branded physical assets at customers' homes work as ongoing marketing.

evidence_quality.rationale: First-hand operator with many specifics (prices, loan terms, truck costs), but revenue and profit are loosely stated, margin is Koerner's rough maths, and churn is estimated rather than measured; the business is under 2 years old.
evidence_quality.promotional_conflict: Koerner promotes his TK Owners community; Spencer sells merch and uses a landing page redirect.
